statement: Make finalize() in codes/loop/loop.sbatch classify a scheduler termination as neither a clean cycle nor a failure. Reproduced offline (evidence/loop_resume/validation_repair_harness.txt scenario K): with the loop running, SIGTERM to the link's process group - what slurmstepd sends at the 2-23:30:00 time limit and on scancel, followed by SIGKILL after KillWait 30 s - makes bash 5.1.8 run the EXIT trap, and finalize logs 'clean exit -- failcount reset to 0' (3 of 3 runs; also when only bash is signalled) or, when the child is signalled first, 'failure rc=143 -- failcount now 1/3' with the successor kept; three links of the latter kind trip the breaker and scancel a healthy chain, and the former resets the breaker on a link whose loop was killed mid-cycle. Second conjunct (scenario L): a loop exit code 3 is treated as a storage stop (successor cancelled, uncounted) even when STOP was not written, so any stage that happens to exit 3 under bash -e ends the chain silently. Fix shape: trap TERM (and optionally an sbatch --signal=B:USR1@N warning) to set a flag before the loop starts; in finalize, when the flag is set or the loop's status is 128+15, log 'scheduler termination', leave .failcount unchanged and keep the successor; treat RC==KTG_RC_SCRATCH_STOP as a chain stop only if $BASEDIR/STOP exists, else count it as a failure. Closes by a result row whose offline injection run adds: SIGTERM to the process group over three consecutive links -> .failcount unchanged, no scancel, successor kept; child-first and bash-only orderings -> the same; loop exit 3 without STOP -> counted as a failure. The executed proof under a real scheduler stays with o25.

statement: codes/loop/loop.sbatch fails OPEN in two places where an integer it relies on cannot be trusted, and in both the breaker stops bounding the chain. (a) Writes. No write of a chain state file is checked (:169, :170, :184, :327, :342, :363; grep for a checked redirect returns nothing), and the reads deliberately fall back to 0 when cat fails, with no WARNING because the fallback 'echo 0' is itself a plain decimal. So when $BASEDIR/.failcount cannot be written -- a directory (X3), chmod 000 (X4), read-only (X5), or more realistically a full quota or a read-only remount -- every failing link reads 0, prints 'failure rc=1 -- failcount now 2/3' then 'chain continues', queues its successor, and the count never advances: a crash loop bounded only by KTG_MAX_CHAIN=200, the o26 class. With .failcount writable but .chain_depth read-only the depth stays at 1 (X6) and the KTG_MAX_CHAIN bound is gone too; with both unwritable there is no bound at all. Reproduced by the validator in evidence/loop_resume/validation_repair4_harness.txt X3-X7: three links each, 'Is a directory' / 'Permission denied' from :169/:184/:363, SBATCH on every link, no SCANCEL. (b) Knobs. KTG_MAX_FAILS, KTG_MAX_CHAIN and KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS are read from the job environment (:100-102, o33 d) and consumed by test(1) and $(( )) without going through read_counter. KTG_MAX_FAILS=abc makes every '-ge' test at :366, :414, :457 return false ('integer expression expected' on stderr), so the breaker NEVER trips: X10b gives 2, 4, 6 over three links with a successor queued each time, and finalize() then aborts at :375 with 'abc: unbound variable' after the write. KTG_MAX_CHAIN=abc removes the depth bound the same way (X10c). KTG_MAX_FAILS=08 aborts finalize() at :375 with 'value too great for base' after the count is written (X10a, the worker's residual): one missing log line, successor kept. Slurm's default --export=ALL carries such a value down the whole chain. Not a value-parsing defect (o35 is discharged): the direction is wrong. A count that cannot be persisted can never stop the chain, and a threshold that cannot be compared never trips, so both must fail CLOSED. Fix shape: (a) check the write at :363 (and the reset writes) and, on failure, say so, treat it as a breaker trip -- touch .breaker_tripped if possible and cancel_successor 'count cannot be persisted' -- and likewise refuse to resubmit when the depth write at :184 fails; (b) pass the three knobs through read_counter at :100-102 and, when the raw value is not what was read, either fall back to the hard-coded default with a WARNING or refuse to chain (the safer choice for KTG_MAX_FAILS, since a zero would trip immediately and a huge value never). Closes by a re-run of X3, X4, X5, X6 (three links each: the successor cancelled on the FIRST link whose count cannot be written, no third link running the loop) and of X10a/X10b/X10c (the breaker trips on link 2 under the fast-failure penalty, or the first link refuses to chain, with a logged line naming the knob and its raw value), with the seed matrix T1-T3 and the regression set unchanged.
